# Backcap

Backcap is a registry of composable backend domains for TypeScript. It lets you install production-ready backend features — authentication, search, blog, billing, notifications — the same way you install npm packages, with full source code written directly into your project. You own every file.

> For the full API reference, see [llms-full.txt](https://faroke.github.io/backcap/llms-full.txt).

## Core Concept

Run `npx @backcap/cli add auth` and Backcap fetches the auth domain from the registry, writes TypeScript source files to `domains/auth/`, installs npm dependencies, and records it in `backcap.json`. No runtime library — the code is yours.

## Three-Layer Architecture

Every Backcap domain uses strict Clean Architecture layering:

- **domain/** — Entities, value objects, domain errors, domain events. Zero external imports. No framework code.
- **application/** — Use cases, port interfaces (TypeScript interfaces), DTOs. Imports domain/ only.
- **contracts/** — Public service interface and factory function. The only barrel index.ts. Imports application/ only.

Import rule: dependencies point inward only. domain/ never imports from application/. application/ never imports from contracts/.

You implement your own adapters on the port interfaces exposed by each domain.

## The Result Pattern

Backcap does not throw errors for expected failures. Every use case returns `Result<T, E>`:

```typescript
const result = await authService.register({ email, password });
if (result.isFail()) {
  const error = result.unwrapError(); // typed error
}
const { userId } = result.unwrap();
```

`Result.ok(value)` / `Result.fail(error)`. Methods: `isOk()`, `isFail()`, `unwrap()`, `unwrapError()`, `map()`.

## CLI Commands

- `npx @backcap/cli init` — Detects framework and package manager, writes backcap.json
- `npx @backcap/cli add <domain>` — Fetches and installs a domain with conflict detection
- `npx @backcap/cli list` — Lists available domains from the registry

## Available Domains (20)

analytics, audit-log, auth, billing, blog, cart, catalog, comments, feature-flags, files, forms, media, notifications, orders, organizations, queues, rbac, search, tags, webhooks

Each domain follows the same three-layer architecture. Install any with `npx @backcap/cli add <name>`.

## Skills (AI Documentation)

Each domain has a SKILL.md with structured frontmatter and file-by-file tables. Load these as AI context before making architectural changes.

## File Naming Conventions

`.entity.ts`, `.vo.ts`, `.error.ts`, `.event.ts`, `.use-case.ts`, `.port.ts`, `.dto.ts`, `.contract.ts`, `.factory.ts` — all kebab-case.

## backcap.json

Configuration file written by `backcap init`:
```json
{
  "framework": "express",
  "packageManager": "pnpm",
  "alias": "@domains",
  "paths": {
    "domains": "domains",
    "skills": ".claude/skills",
    "shared": "shared"
  }
}
```
